anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet, REG1 (MIC26903YJL-TR) pin 30, named PGND_7, is wired to the REG_SW (switching-node) net instead of GND. Every other power-ground pin of the same device (pins 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 21) is tied to GND, and the switch-node pins (4, 9, 10, 11, 12, 28) are tied to REG_SW — pin 30 is the lone PGND pin merged into the switching node.
anomalies.expected: All PGND pins of the buck regulator must connect to the power ground, which the spec explicitly requires to be kept separate from signal ground and joined at only one point ('Keep SGND and PGND separate - connect only at one location!'). PGND_7 (pin 30) should terminate at GND, not at the inductor/switch node.

evidence.quote: Power sheet, REG1 MIC26903YJL-TR: '30 PGND_7' connected by wire to net label 'REG_SW' (same net as SW_1–SW_6 and L1); pins 2/5/6/7/8/21 PGND_x connect to GND symbols
"Keep SGND and PGND separate - connect only at one location!" — an explicit single-point star-ground instruction on the power sheet
"A MIC26903YJL-TR synchronous buck regulator steps the battery input down to 5 V"

anomalies.impact: The regulator's power-ground pin is driven by the full VIN-to-GND switching waveform of the SW node. The buck loses its ground reference, so the 5 V rail cannot regulate (or is severely corrupted), and the downstream LD39200 3V3 rail, servos, GPS, and USB bridges lose their supply; the IC is likely damaged by the ground-pin being swung to VIN.

parsed.summary: The schematic otherwise matches the specification (correct MCUs, sensors, regulators, addresses, and the documented barometer RESET/EOC mix-up), but on the Power sheet the MIC26903 buck's PGND_7 pin (REG1.30) is tied to the switching node REG_SW instead of ground, shorting the power ground to the inductor node and breaking the 5 V rail.
